constants.name: text_end
constants.comment: The byte that ends TITLE's text

subroutines.name: title_start
subroutines.title: TITLE: draw the title page and wait for a key
subroutines.description: The title page between the intro and the game. PLOAD runs it with */, the next file on the tape; the file's execution address is title_entry, two instructions into the loop that sends mode_vdu, not this LDX #0 (see title_entry). The run is a straight line in four phases, marked by block comments below. Screen: MODE 5 with colour 2 blue, then stripe_pattern copied into every character cell from &5800 to &7FFF. Picture: title_picture, &A00 bytes, copied a byte at a time over character rows 1-8. Text: page_text (the credits, the title in a black window and a white window of text), then blank_line_text unless INKEY(-256) reports an Electron, then black_window_vdu. End: *TAPE, then */ runs the next file on the tape, DUNK, whose loader brings in the rest of the game and does not return.

banners.name: stripe_pattern
banners.title: Background stripe pattern
banners.description: TITLE is the title page the cassette shows between its intro and the game: PLOAD runs it with */, the next file on the tape, and it ends by running the next file after it, DUNK. Its data comes first and the code, title_start (&28C6), after it; title_start's banner describes the run. This first table is one MODE 5 character cell, copied over the whole screen: even pixel rows black (&00), odd rows four pixels of colour 2 (&F0), which mode_vdu makes blue.

banners.name: mode_vdu
banners.title: VDU codes: MODE 5, colour 2 blue
banners.description: Eight bytes sent by title_start before anything is drawn: VDU 22,5 (MODE 5) and VDU 19,2,4,0,0,0 (logical colour 2 shows as blue).

banners.name: page_text
banners.title: VDU codes: credits, title and keys
banners.description: Printed by title_start up to the &FF terminator. The credits go at fixed text positions on the striped background; the title is printed in a text window cleared to black at columns 6-13, rows 10-12; a note to see the inlay card in a window cleared to white at columns 1-18, rows 18-24, in black text, as four lines of 18 characters.

banners.name: blank_line_text
banners.title: Text: a line of spaces
banners.description: Eighteen spaces and the &FF terminator, the width of the white window. title_start prints them after its text on any machine but an Electron; they fall on the window's next line, which is already white.

banners.name: black_window_vdu
banners.title: VDU codes: an empty black window
banners.description: Printed last: a text window at columns 2-17, rows 26-28, cleared to black with white text. TITLE prints nothing in it, and the loader that runs next, Dunjunz1, selects MODE 2.

banners.name: tape_command
banners.title: Commands: select the cassette and run the next file
banners.description: Two CR-terminated OSCLI commands, *TAPE and */, that title_start issues at the end. */ with no name runs the next file on the tape, DUNK.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Zeros up to the picture, which starts on a page boundary.

banners.name: title_picture
banners.title: The title picture
banners.description: Eight MODE 5 character rows (&A00 bytes, &140 a row, eight bytes a cell, top pixel row first), copied by title_start to character rows 1-8. A blue frame holds a white panel at the left, the name BUG BYTE in large white letters and a red and blue face at the right.

memory_map.name: copy_from
memory_map.description: Source pointer, low byte: stripe_pattern while striping, then the next byte of title_picture.

memory_map.name: copy_to
memory_map.description: Screen pointer, low byte: the next character cell while striping, then the next screen byte of the picture.

memory_map.name: mode5_screen
memory_map.description: The start of MODE 5's screen memory (&5800-&7FFF)

memory_map.name: title_picture_screen
memory_map.description: Character row 1 of the MODE 5 screen, where the logo picture is copied (&5940-&633F)

comments_before_label: The file's execution address, where */ enters TITLE: the INX of the loop that sends mode_vdu, two instructions after title_start's LDX #0. So the loop starts from whatever X the MOS enters with, plus one, and sends from mode_vdu + X until X wraps round to 8. Run from PLOAD on MOS 1.20, X is &E4, so 27 bytes of this code (&28ED-&2907) go to the VDU drivers first: a few characters and a VDU 24 that sets a graphics window, both undone by the MODE 5 that follows intact.
Screen, with MODE 5 set: stripe all of it, &5800-&7FFF, one character cell at a time.
